s1.syndrome_frame: Neurocutaneous disorder with seizures and multiple congenital anomalies
salient_findings: Massive neoplasm formation in posterior cranial fossa
key_facts: Patient is a 12-month-old boy
Presented with convulsive seizures
Seizures characterized by faltering, smirking with withdrawal of the head and eyes
Had a blond hair strand at birth
Had polydactyly of the right hand at birth
Had cardiac rhabdomyoma at birth
Depigmented spots appeared on torso at 4 months
First convulsive seizures noted at 8 months
Psychomotor development was normal for age
No family history of similar conditions
Brain CT scan showed massive neoplasm formation in posterior cranial fossa
Brain MRI with contrast revealed extracranial solid mass in posterior fossa with brain stem compression
Genetic testing revealed TSC1 gene mutation

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has characteristic features of TSC, including seizures, depigmented spots, polydactyly, and cardiac rhabdomyoma, with a confirmed TSC1 gene mutation

shortlist.label: Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a brain mass in the posterior cranial fossa with brain stem compression, consistent with SEGA, a common tumor in TSC

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has seizures and depigmented spots, which can be seen in SWS, although the presence of a TSC1 gene mutation makes TSC more likely

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple congenital anomalies and seizures, which can be seen in NF1, although the absence of cafe-au-lait spots and other characteristic features makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has seizures and a brain mass, which can be seen in HME, although the presence of a TSC1 gene mutation and other characteristic features of TSC makes it less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of convulsive seizures, blond hair strand, polydactyly, cardiac rhabdomyoma, and depigmented spots, along with imaging findings of tubers, subcortical tubers, and triventricular hydrocephalus, and a TSC1 gene mutation, are all characteristic features of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

rejected.label: Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a brain tumor, the presence of multiple other features such as polydactyly, cardiac rhabdomyoma, and depigmented spots point more towards a systemic condition like Tuberous Sclerosis Complex rather than a single tumor type.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a port-wine stain, which is not mentioned, and does not typically include features like polydactyly or cardiac rhabdomyoma.

rejected.label: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
rejected.why: The lack of cafe-au-lait spots and other diagnostic criteria for NF1, along with the presence of TSC1 gene mutation, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Hemimegalencephaly
rejected.why: While this condition involves brain malformation, it does not account for the extracranial features like polydactyly, cardiac rhabdomyoma, or the specific genetic mutation found in this patient.
